name: Real asset income investing
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Contracted Real Asset Income
caseLead: The investment case rests on property, utility and infrastructure assets that collect contracted rents and regulated tariffs, so their income is more predictable than the earnings of most companies. The income persists because new assets are slow and costly to build, licences and regulation limit competition, and many contracts pass inflation through to revenue, which matters when energy prices or trade policy raise costs.
caseRest: The main risk is a rise in real interest rates, because the value of long-lived cash flows falls when the discount rate rises. Income can stay stable while asset values fall sharply, as in 2022 when listed property fell as yields rose even though rents continued to grow. Debt adds to the risk, because owners that must refinance at higher rates pass part of their income to lenders.
figNote: The large figure on each card shows the change in the 10-year US Treasury yield over the episode, in basis points, where 100 basis points equal one percentage point. Real assets are valued by discounting long-lived income, so a rise in yields usually lowers their prices and a fall raises them.

events.title: Taper signal lifts yields and hits real assets
events.text: The Federal Reserve signalled in May 2013 that it would slow bond purchases, and the 10-year yield rose about 135 basis points by September. The strategy lost because higher yields lowered the value of rent and utility cash flows.

events.title: Brexit pushes yields to record lows
events.text: The 10-year yield fell about 90 basis points from December 2015 to a record low of 1.4% in July 2016, after the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union. The strategy gained because lower yields raised the value of stable rental and regulated income.

events.title: Covid sell-off hits property and infrastructure
events.text: The 10-year yield fell about 140 basis points from December to 9 March 2020, but listed property and infrastructure shares fell sharply as tenants lost income. The strategy lost because lower yields did not offset the risk of unpaid rent and weaker traffic volumes.

events.title: Rate rises lower the value of property assets
events.text: The Federal Reserve began raising rates in March 2022, and the 10-year yield rose about 235 basis points over the year. The strategy lost because higher yields lowered property values, although inflation-linked rents and regulated tariffs limited the fall in income.

events.title: Fed signals cuts and yields fall sharply
events.text: The 10-year yield fell about 110 basis points from its October peak to the end of 2023 after the Federal Reserve signalled rate cuts. The strategy gained because lower yields raised the value of property and infrastructure cash flows.

events.title: US tariffs raise costs and lift yields
events.text: The 10-year yield rose about 48 basis points in the week to 11 April 2025 as tariffs raised inflation concerns. Results were mixed because infrastructure with inflation-linked revenue held its value, while property shares fell with higher yields.

instrument: Global listed property, utility and infrastructure shares; reviewed quarterly; distributions reinvested
rules: Assets selected for contracted or regulated income, average lease or concession length above 5 years and net debt below 6 times earnings; no asset above 5%
costs: Estimated commissions, bid-ask spreads and withholding tax on distributions
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from contracted income to interest rate control

legs.position: Listed property companies with long leases

legs.purpose: Earns regulated returns linked to inflation

entry: Income cover above 1.3 times and net debt below 6 times earnings
size: No holding above 5%; set to a 10% annualised volatility target
exit: Position reduced when income cover falls below 1.1 times
stop: Share weight halved if the 10-year real yield rises 100 basis points in six months
marketWatch: Rehyn monitors the 10-year real yield, the gap between asset income yields and government bond yields, and net debt against earnings, because these show how sensitive asset values are to financing costs. Central bank rate decisions, inflation releases and changes in energy or trade policy are the events that matter most. A rise in real yields would weigh on valuations, while contracted income would continue to support cash flow.

favourable.heading: Falling real yields
favourable.text: Falling real yields favour the strategy because lower discount rates raise the value of long-lived income. After the Federal Reserve signalled rate cuts in December 2023, the 10-year yield fell about 110 basis points from its October peak and listed property rallied strongly.

favourable.heading: Inflation-linked revenue
favourable.text: Inflation pass-through favours the strategy because rents, tariffs and tolls rise with prices, which protects income when costs increase. In 2022 US consumer prices rose about 6.5% over the year and regulated utilities and toll road operators raised revenue, so infrastructure held up better than the equity market.

favourable.heading: Stable credit conditions
favourable.text: Stable credit conditions favour the strategy because owners refinance debt at manageable rates, so income reaches investors instead of lenders. Between 2012 and 2019 low borrowing costs allowed property and infrastructure owners to extend debt maturities and raise distributions.

adverse.heading: Rising real interest rates
adverse.text: Rising real yields hurt the strategy because higher discount rates lower the present value of long-lived income. In 2022 the 10-year yield rose about 235 basis points and listed property fell sharply even though rents continued to grow.

adverse.heading: Tenant stress and lockdowns
adverse.text: A sudden loss of tenant income hurts the strategy because rent and traffic revenue can stop while debt payments continue. In March 2020 retail, hotel and airport assets lost income as lockdowns began, so listed real assets fell sharply.

adverse.heading: Tighter credit and refinancing
adverse.text: Tighter credit hurts the strategy because owners that must refinance debt pay higher interest, which absorbs income that would otherwise be distributed. After the 2013 taper signal, borrowing costs rose and listed property and utilities fell as higher yields fed through to refinancing costs.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each figure includes the distributions received during the event window.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in Treasury yields, listed property and utility shares and inflation expectations, which are then applied to the strategy's current holdings.

related.why: Owns infrastructure with revenue linked to inflation. Bears regulatory and political risk, with returns tied to price growth.
Buys listed property below appraised value. Bears the risk that the discount persists or widens when yields rise.
